questions.question: Which of the following banks is in charge of India’s banking and monetary system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RBI**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the central bank of India, which is responsible for the regulation of the monetary and banking system in the country.
 
• RBI was established on **1st April 1935** in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The bank is responsible for issuing currency, controlling inflation, managing the country's foreign exchange and gold reserves, and ensuring financial stability.
 
• RBI also plays a key role in the development of the financial infrastructure necessary for the economic growth of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **headquarters** of RBI is located in **Mumbai, Maharashtra**.
 
• The RBI's affairs are governed by a central board of directors. The board is appointed by the Government of India.
 
• RBI is also the regulator of the financial system and ensures that the credit needs of the economy are met and that financial markets operate efficiently.
 
• The bank also plays a significant role in the development of the country's financial infrastructure, including the establishment of institutions like NABARD, SIDBI, and NHB.
 
• RBI conducts monetary policy with the aim of maintaining price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.

• **These are small loans that are typically provided to low-income individuals or entrepreneurs who do not have access to traditional banking services.**

questions.question: Selling of bonds by the RBI will cause money supply to __________.

options.text: No relationship exists between selling bonds and money supply

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**decrease**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Selling of bonds by the RBI** will cause the money supply to **decrease**.
 
• This is because when the RBI sells bonds, it takes money out of circulation, thereby reducing the overall money supply in the economy.
 
• The reduction in money supply can lead to higher interest rates as there is less money available for borrowing.
 
• This is a monetary policy tool used by the RBI to control inflation and stabilize the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the central banking institution of India, which controls the issuance and supply of the Indian rupee.
 
• It also manages the country's main payment systems and works to promote its economic development.
 
• The RBI was established on April 1, 1935, in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The primary objective of the RBI is to maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
 
• It employs various monetary policy tools, including open market operations, to regulate the money supply in the economy.
 
• Selling government bonds is one of the open market operations that the RBI uses to control liquidity.

questions.question: Reserve ratio and money supply have ________ relationship.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a negative**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Reserve ratio and money supply have **a negative** relationship.
 
• The reserve ratio is the portion of depositors' balances that banks must have on hand as cash. This is a regulatory requirement set by central banks.
 
• When the reserve ratio is increased, banks have less money to lend out, which reduces the money supply in the economy.
 
• Conversely, when the reserve ratio is decreased, banks can lend more money, which increases the money supply.
 
• This relationship is crucial for central banks when they aim to control inflation and stabilize the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The reserve ratio is a tool used in monetary policy to regulate the banking system and control the money supply.
 
• Other tools include open market operations and the discount rate.
 
• The reserve ratio is part of the broader set of policies known as reserve requirements.
 
• Changes in the reserve ratio can have significant impacts on the economy, influencing interest rates, borrowing, and spending.
 
• Central banks, such as the Federal Reserve in the United States or the Reserve Bank of India, adjust the reserve ratio as part of their efforts to maintain economic stability.

questions.question: In 1991, the Indian rupee was devalued in how many steps?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Twice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian rupee had two rounds of devaluation in 1991, beginning on **July 1 and ending on July 3.**
 
• Indian Rupee was devalued for the third time in 1991.
 
 
• The devaluation procedure in 1991 was carried out in two steps on July 1 and July 3.
 
• The year 1991 is often cited as the year of economic reform in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

__
 
• ** In total Indian rupee **was devalued **three times**, as per the question in **1991 Indian rupee was devalued twice.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Reserve Bank of India issues currency notes in India.
 
• The Indian rupee became an independent currency with the establishment of RBI in 1935.
 
• Reserve Bank of India issues all currency notes above one rupee.
 
• Indian Rupee was devalued in three instances but four times.
 
• Indian Rupee was devalued for the **first time in 1949.**
 
• Indian Rupee was devalued for the **second time in 1966__.**
 
 
• India’s war with Pakistan in late 1965 played a key role in the 1966 devaluation.
 
• It was the result of the first major financial crisis the government faced.
 
• Inflation had caused Indian prices to become much higher than world prices at the pre-devaluation exchange rate.
 
• There was foreign pressure on India to reform its economy.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an example of intermediate goods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__4) Medicine__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Intermediate Goods:**

 
 
• Intermediate goods are products used as inputs in the production of other goods. They are not final goods and are typically transformed or assembled into final products.
 
 
 
• **Hard Drive:** **This is an intermediate good.**
 
 
• A hard drive is used in the production of computers and other electronic devices. It is not sold as a final product but as a component of a final product.
 
 
 
• **Steel:** **This is an intermediate good.**
 
 
• Steel is used in the production of various products like cars, machinery, and buildings. It is a raw material that gets transformed into finished goods.
 
 
 
• **Paint:** **This is an intermediate good.**
 
 
• Paint is used in manufacturing and construction processes to finish and protect surfaces. It is not a final product by itself but is used in the production of finished goods.
 
 
 
• **Medicine:** **This is not an intermediate good.**
 
 
• Medicine is a final good that is consumed directly by individuals for health purposes. It is not used as an input in the production of other goods.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Examples of Intermediate Goods:**

 
 
• Other examples of intermediate goods include flour used in baking, wood used in furniture making, and glass used in window manufacturing.

questions.question: A government budget shows a primary deficit of Rs. 6,900 crore. The revenue expenditure on interest payment is Rs. 400 crore. Fiscal deficit is equal to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs. 7,300 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To calculate the fiscal deficit, we need to consider both the primary deficit and the interest payments on debt.

**Fiscal Deficit = Primary Deficit + Interest Payments**

Primary Deficit = Rs. 6,900 crore

Interest Payments = Rs. 400 crore

Fiscal Deficit = 6,900 crore + 400 crore

Fiscal Deficit = Rs. 7,300 crore

 
• Therefore, the **fiscal deficit is Rs. 7,300 crore.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **A fiscal deficit **occurs when a government spends more than it receives in a given year. It's calculated by subtracting total income from total expenditure.
 
• The result can be expressed in absolute terms or as a percentage of the GDP.
 
• A government can close the gap between income and spending by borrowing. A fiscal deficit is different from fiscal debt, which is the total debt accumulated over years of deficit spending.
 
• It's also different from fiscal imbalance, which is a measure of future difference between.
 
• A fiscal deficit is not universally regarded as a negative event. An expansionary fiscal policy leads to higher budget deficits while a contractionary policy reduces deficits.

questions.question: Expenditure of the government on health facilities, education and fixed-asset acquisition is termed as _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**capital expenditure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Capital expenditure**, the allocation of government funds for the **enhancement of health facilities, education, and fixed-asset acquisition,** plays a pivotal role in fostering economic growth.
 
• This expenditure encompasses investments in physical assets like** infrastructure, buildings, machinery, and equipment,** aimed at bolstering the productive capacity of the economy.
 
• Allocated through the annual budget, presented by the finance minister, capital expenditure is viewed as a productive investment that generates future income and employment opportunities.
 
• Notably, for the **fiscal year 2024-2025, **there has been an **11.1% increase in the capital expenditure** outlay, with a total allocation of Rs 11,11,111 crore, constituting 3.4% of the GDP.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Revenue Expenditure** encompasses the day-to-day operational expenses essential for sustaining the continuous activities of a business or government entity. These expenses cover various aspects such as salaries, utilities, rent, raw materials, and maintenance costs.
 
• **Plan Expenditure **constitutes the government's expenditure allocated for specific developmental projects and schemes as outlined in its planned development programs. These expenditures are aimed at achieving targeted growth and development objectives.
 
• **Non-Plan Revenue Expenditure** includes all other expenses incurred by the government that are not directly associated with planned developmental activities. This category encompasses routine administrative expenses, interest payments on loans, subsidies, and other recurring expenditures.

questions.question: Assume that the value of the cash reserve ratio is 25%. What will be the value of money multiplier?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The value of the **cash reserve ratio** (CRR) is **25%**.
 
• The **money multiplier** is calculated as the reciprocal of the cash reserve ratio.
 
• Formula: **Money Multiplier = 1 / CRR**
 
• Given that CRR is 25%, the money multiplier is calculated as follows:
 
• **Money Multiplier = 1 / 0.25 = 4**
 
• Therefore, the value of the money multiplier is **4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **cash reserve ratio** (CRR) is a percentage of a bank's total deposits that must be maintained with the central bank as reserves.
 
• The **money multiplier** effect describes how an initial deposit can lead to a larger final increase in the total money supply.
 
• A higher CRR means a lower money multiplier and vice versa.
 
• The central bank uses CRR as a tool to control liquidity in the banking system.

questions.question: Capital adequacy ratio for a NBFC – MFI is ______.

options.text: 15% of the aggregate risk weighted assets
11% of the aggregate risk weighted assets

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15% of the aggregate risk-weighted assets.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Microfinance institutions MFIs**, are businesses that **lend money and offer other financial services** to the **less fortunate members** of society.
 
• **Rural areas and low-income populations **in metropolitan areas are their **primary target markets** for modest loans.
 
• Some** MFIs** that meet specific requirements and are** non-deposit-taking organization**s are regulated and** overseen by the RBI.**
 
• The **Non-Banking Financial Company-Microfinance Institutions (NBFC MFI)** are the **"Last Mile Financiers."**
 
• To make these NBFC MFIs **healthy and responsible**, they were included **under the RBI.**
 
• Every new NBFC MFI must maintain a** Capital adequacy ratio o**f at least **15% of its aggregate risk-weighted assets.**
 
• It shall include** Tier I and Tier II Capital.**
 
• After total, the amount of **Tier II capital **must n**ot exceed 100% of Tier I capital**
 
• The **CRAR for NBFC-MFI** having more than **25% loan portfolio **in **Andhra Pradesh** will be at **12% only for the years 2011-2012.**
 
• Afterwards, it is mandatory to **maintain up to 15% CRAR.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Each new **NBFC-MFI **is required to maintain an **aggregate cap**, which should not **exceed 12%**. 
 
• The interest rate on **each individual loan** must be computed on a declining balance basis and **cannot be greater than 26% p.a.**
 
• NBFC-MFIs are permitted to lend to any** individual borrower**, even if that borrower is not a part of a **joint liability group (JLG) or self-help organization.**
 
• The guidelines state that an NBFC-MFI must examine the **back office operations**.​

questions.question: A money bill under Article 111 of the Constitution of India, presented to the President for assent, has to be endorsed by a Certificate of the ______ signed by him/her that it is a money bill.

options.text: Secretary General of the Rajya Sabha
Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
Secretary General of the Lok Sabha

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speaker of the Lok Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A money bill under** Article 111 of the Constitution of India,** presented to the President for assent, has to be endorsed by a Certificate of the **Speaker of the Lok Sabha** signed by him/her that it is a money bill.
 
• The money bill's certificate is approved by the Speaker of the House of People. It says that it's a money bill and is signed by him/her.
 
• When it is submitted to the President for ratification under article 111 and sent to the Council of States under article 109, it is considered endorsed.
 
• Article 110 of the Indian Constitution defines money bill. Money bills deal with money-related issues such as taxes and public spending. 
 
• The lower chamber of the Indian Parliament is called the Lok Sabha, and its speaker is its highest authority and presiding official.
 
• In the Lok Sabha's first meeting after the general elections, the speaker is chosen by the whole assembly. The speaker, who holds a five-year term, is selected among the Lok Sabha's current members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Rajya Sabha Secretariat's** administrative head is the Secretary General of the Rajya Sabha. The Vice President of India, who chairs the Rajya Sabha, appoints the secretary general.
 
• When the **Rajya Sabha chairperson** (the vice president of India) is not present, the deputy chairman of the Rajya Sabha preside over the proceedings of the Rajya Sabha. The Rajya Sabha internally elects the deputy chairman.
 
• The administrative head of the** Lok Sabha Secretariat **is the Secretary General of the Lok Sabha. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha appoints the secretary general.

questions.question: If the value/percentage of the cash reserve ratio falls, then the value of money multiplier ________.

__
 
• The **money multiplier** represents how much the money supply in the economy can increase with a given increase in bank reserves.
 
• A **lower CRR** means that banks are required to keep less cash in reserves, **allowing them to lend more money**.
 
• As banks lend more, **the creation of money in the economy increases**, thus** raising the value of the money multiplier.**
 
• In addition, when the CRR decreases, banks have more funds available for lending, this increase in lending further amplifies the money supply, thereby **enhancing the overall liquidity in the financial system.**

questions.question: If tax rate decreases with increase in taxable base, then this type of taxation is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**regressive.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A regressive tax system is one in which the **tax rate decreases as the taxable amount (or income) increases.**
 
• In a regressive system, lower-income individuals pay a higher percentage of their income in taxes than higher-income individuals. 
 
• Regressive taxes can lead to** increased income inequality.**
 
• Examples of Regressive Taxes: **Sales Taxes, Excise Taxes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Progressive Taxation**:

 
 
• This tax system imposes a** higher tax rate on higher-income earners.**
 
• As income increases, so does the tax rate, ensuring that wealthier individuals pay a larger proportion of their income in taxes.
 
 
 
• **Degressive taxation**
 
 
• It is a hybrid tax system** combining regressive and proportional taxation elements.**
 
• In a degressive tax system, the tax rate decreases as the income or taxable base increases, but not as drastically as in a regressive tax system.
 
• It starts with a progressive rate for lower income levels but eventually flattens out, so the tax burden becomes less steep for higher income brackets.
 
 
 
• **Increasing tax rate** system is the** same as progressive taxation.**

questions.question: How much percentage of the capital of MUDRA is contributed by SIDBI?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **100%** of the capital of MUDRA is contributed by SIDBI.
 
• MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency) was established to provide funding to the non-corporate small business sector.
 
• SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India) is the principal financial institution for the promotion, financing, and development of the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprise (MSME) sector.
 
• SIDBI provides refinance support to banks and other financial institutions for lending to micro units under MUDRA.
 
• The contribution by SIDBI ensures that MUDRA has a strong financial backing to support its objectives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MUDRA** was launched on **8th April 2015** by the Government of India.
 
• Its primary objective is to provide loans at low rates to micro-finance institutions and non-banking financial institutions which then provide credit to MSMEs.
 
• MUDRA operates under the aegis of **Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)**.
 
• Loans provided under MUDRA are classified into three categories: **Shishu** (loans up to ₹50,000), **Kishore** (loans from ₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh), and **Tarun** (loans from ₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh).
 
• The initiative aims to provide financial support to small businesses and entrepreneurs who are often unable to access formal banking channels.

questions.question: For which of the following sources of financial resources may financial intermediation NOT be required?

options.text: Borrowing from All India Development Financial Institutions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Family funds**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Family funds** are financial resources that can be obtained directly from family members without the need for financial intermediation.
 
• In contrast, raising equity via public offering, borrowing from banks, and borrowing from All India Development Financial Institutions typically require the involvement of financial intermediaries.
 
• Financial intermediation involves institutions such as banks, investment funds, and development financial institutions that facilitate the channeling of funds from savers to borrowers.
 
• Using family funds can be advantageous as it may involve lower costs and fewer formalities compared to institutional financing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial intermediation** is a process by which financial institutions accept savings from individuals and lend them to others, facilitating the allocation of resources in the economy.
 
• Common financial intermediaries include **banks, credit unions, insurance companies, and investment firms**.
 
• Direct financing, such as using family funds, bypasses these intermediaries and can be a quicker way to secure necessary funds.
 
• However, relying solely on family funds may limit the amount of capital available compared to institutional sources.

questions.question: In which year was the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) set up?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1990**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)** serves as the apex regulatory body for overseeing the licensing and regulation of micro, small, and medium enterprise finance companies in India.
 
• It operates under the purview of the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, with its headquarters located in Lucknow and offices across the country.
 
• Established on April 2, 1990, by the Government of India, SIDBI initially operated as a wholly owned subsidiary of IDBI Bank. However, it was delinked from IDBI on March 27, 2000.
 
• SIDBI's primary objective is to provide refinance facilities to banks and financial institutions, as well as offer term lending and working capital finance to industries, particularly those in the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector.
 
• SIDBI coordinates the activities of institutions involved in similar endeavors. Its establishment in 1990 was facilitated through an Act of Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• SIDBI is among the five All India Financial Institutions overseen by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI).**
 
• The other four institutions include the Export-Import Bank of India (Exim Bank), National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), National Housing Bank (NHB), and National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NABFID).
 
• NHB came under government control after the government acquired more than a 51% stake in it. These institutions play a crucial statutory role in the financial markets, particularly through credit extension and refinancing operations, catering to the long-term financing requirements of the industrial sector. SIDBI actively contributes to the development of Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs) through the SIDBI Foundation for Micro Credit.
 
• It supports the extension of microfinance through the Micro Finance Institution (MFI) route, demonstrating its commitment to fostering financial inclusion and supporting the growth of small businesses.

questions.question: Which of the following funds was created in 2005 to channelise funds received from disinvestment proceeds of PSUs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Investment Fund.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Investment Fund**** **was created in** 2005 to channelize funds **received from disinvestment proceeds of PSUs.
 
• The NIF was constituted by the Government of India in November 2005.
 
• It was set for channelizing the proceeds from the disinvestment of Central Public Sector Enterprises are channelized into it.
 
• The corpus of NIF is of a permanent nature.
 
• The money with the NIF is permanent in nature and NIF is professionally managed to provide returns to the Government, without depleting its value.
 
• The NIF is professionally managed by some selected Public Sector Mutual Funds (like UTI Asset Management Company Ltd., SBI Funds Management Private Ltd.) and LIC Mutual Fund Asset Management Company Ltd., to provide sustainable returns to the Government, without depleting the corpus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The consolidated fund is filled by the Direct and indirect taxes Loans taken by the Indian government and returning of loans/interests of loans to the government by anyone/agency that has taken it.

 
 
• The government needs parliamentary approval to withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund.
 
• The provision for a Consolidated fund is given in Article 266(1) of the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• The provision for the Contingency fund is given in Article 267(1) of the Constitution of India.
 
 
• Its fixed corpus is Rs. 500 crores.
 
 
 
• Public Accounts of India is constituted under Article 266(2) of the Constitution.
 
 
• The government does not need permission to take advances from a public account.

questions.question: Which of the following is a selective credit instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Credit rationing**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Credit rationing** is a selective credit instrument used by central banks to control the amount of credit that is available to the economy.
 
• This tool is used to ensure that credit is directed towards essential sectors and activities, thereby influencing the allocation of resources in the economy.
 
• Unlike tools like the Bank Rate or CRR, which affect the overall credit conditions in the economy, credit rationing specifically targets certain sectors or types of credit.
 
• This method can be particularly useful during times of economic stress or when certain sectors are deemed to be of strategic importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Variable reserve ratio** refers to the changing reserve requirements that banks must hold, which influences their ability to lend money.
 
• **Bank rate** is the rate at which the central bank lends money to commercial banks, influencing the overall level of interest rates in the economy.
 
• **CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio)** is the percentage of a bank's total deposits that must be maintained with the central bank in the form of liquid cash.
 
• Selective credit control measures like credit rationing are part of the broader monetary policy toolkit used by central banks to achieve economic stability and growth.

questions.question: Taxes like gift tax, wealth tax etc are also referred to as which type of taxes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Direct taxes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct taxes** are taxes that are paid directly to the government by the individual or organization on whom it is imposed.
 
• Examples of direct taxes include **gift tax, wealth tax, income tax,** etc.
 
• These taxes are generally progressive, meaning the rate increases as the taxable amount increases.
 
• Direct taxes are considered more equitable because they are based on the ability-to-pay principle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Direct taxes are administered and collected by the **Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)** in India.
 
• The CBDT is a part of the Department of Revenue under the Ministry of Finance.
 
• Direct taxes play a critical role in the revenue generation of a country and are used for various public services and infrastructure development.
 
• Unlike indirect taxes, direct taxes cannot be shifted to another person or entity.
 
• Compliance with direct tax regulations is mandatory for all eligible taxpayers to avoid penalties and legal actions.

questions.question: ________ is the currency in the hands of the public plus commercial bank reserves, also called ‘high-powered money’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monetary base.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• High-powered money is a** macroeconomic term** pertaining to the financial base, which is controlled by the institution in a country that **controls financial policy.**
 
• This is generally either the** finance ministry or the central bank.**
 
• The financial base is called high-powered because the magnitude of changes in the financial base is greatly magnified by the plutocrat multiplier.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Desired reserve ratio:**

 
 
• The reserve ratio is an important tool of the monetary policy of an economy and plays an essential role in regulating the money supply.
 
• When the central bank wants to increase the money supply in the economy, it lowers the reserve ratio.
 
• As a result, commercial banks have higher funds to disburse as loans, thereby increasing the money supply in an economy.
 
 
 
• **Excess reserve:**
 
 
• Excess reserves are capital reserves held by a bank or financial institution in excess of what's needed by controllers, creditors, or internal controls.
 
• For marketable banks, redundant reserves are measured against standard reserve demand quantities set by central banking authorities.
 
 
 
• **Money multiplier:**
 
 
• The phenomenon in which money is created in the form of the creation of credits in the economy is referred to as the money multiplier and is based on the fractional reserve banking system.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a revenue receipt by the government?

options.text: Cash grants-in-aid from foreign countries and international organisations
Fees and other receipts for services rendered by the government
Dividends and profits on investments made by the government

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Sale of government assets**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Government revenue is the money that the government receives through taxes and non-tax sources to undertake government expenditures. 
 
• It is classified into revenue receipts and capital receipts. 
 
• Examples of revenue receipts are 
 
 
• Cash grants-in-aid from foreign countries and international organizations.
 
• Fees and other receipts for services rendered by the government.
 
• Dividends and profits on investments made by the government.
 
 
 
• ​The sale of government assets is part of capital receipts.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Features of revenue receipts 

 
• The revenue receipts are recurring in nature.
 
• It does not create any liability for the government.
 
• It should not lead to a fall in the assets of the government.
 
• The revenue receipts are non-redeemable 
 
• It can be further classified into tax revenue and non-tax revenue.

46
